name: bm-r4-coupled-2d-epithelium
title: Coupled 2D epithelial sheet
claim: The explicit 2D epithelial sheet relaxes under the Tyssue vertex model and yields finite, uniform per-cell geometry: all 12 cell-faces carry the same basal area (5.0) and the same explicit cell height (1.93), and stepping the EulerSolver keeps that geometry finite. The figure-level comparison of this spatial confinement to the homogeneous R1 baseline, and the explicit BM-traction coupling, are not yet in the composite.
experiment: Build the tyssue_2d_sheet composite (an explicit polygonal CrossSection sheet over the vivarium-tyssue engine, each cell-face carrying an explicit height degree of freedom) and step the EulerSolver. Reconstruct the mesh counts (faces = cells, vertices), read every cell-face basal area and explicit height off face_df, and confirm the geometry stays finite and positive across several Euler steps (dt 0.01). This is a qualitative spatial-engine check -- that the sheet resolves and relaxes to finite per-cell geometry -- not yet a quantitative confinement comparison to R1.
result: The 2D sheet resolves and relaxes deterministically. The mesh carries 12 cell-faces (faces = cells), 12 cells and 24 vertices on a flat z=0 plane spanning +/-5.80 in x and y. Every cell-face relaxes to the same basal area, 5.0, and the same explicit cell height, 1.9319, with all face areas and heights finite. Stepping the EulerSolver five times (dt 0.01) keeps per-cell area and height finite and positive with no NaN or blow-up. The homogeneous cell is uniform because the sheet carries no heterogeneous growth, division or cortical-tension variation yet, and the BM traction/area law is not wired as an explicit coupling -- so the spatial-vs-homogeneous confinement comparison to R1 is a followup, not a result here.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition: The explicit 2D sheet resolves over the tyssue engine and relaxes to finite per-cell geometry, so it can serve as the planar spatial substrate the 3D monolayer (R5) builds on. Advancing to the quantitative confinement claim additionally requires the BM-traction coupling and the homogeneous-vs-spatial comparison to R1, which are flagged as followups.

question: Do the paper's confinement regimes survive explicit cell topology and heterogeneous growth in a spatial 2D epithelium?

purpose.question: Do the paper's confinement regimes survive explicit cell topology and heterogeneous growth in a spatial 2D epithelium?
purpose.mechanism: A Tyssue polygonal sheet carries an explicit per-cell basal area and an explicit cell-height degree of freedom (rather than the inferred prism relation of the homogeneous R1 model). The vertex-model EulerSolver relaxes the sheet; a BM traction/area law (calibrated from R2) is intended to resist basal-area growth, reproducing the R1 confinement response in the homogeneous limit before heterogeneous growth and division are added.
purpose.expected_outcome: The sheet relaxes to finite, well-posed per-cell geometry (areas and heights), establishing the spatial substrate; the homogeneous limit should later match R1's confinement response once the BM traction is coupled.

key_assumptions: The sheet is an explicit polygonal CrossSection: each cell-face carries its own basal area and an explicit cell-height degree of freedom, not an inferred volume/area prism relation.
The current composite is a homogeneous relaxation: no heterogeneous growth, cell division or cortical-tension variation is applied, so all cells relax to the same geometry.
Reduced units throughout (areas, heights, lengths are dimensionless); no calibration to microns is claimed.

The BM traction/area law (calibrated from R2) is NOT wired as an explicit coupling in this composite; the effective constitutive BM and an explicit LAMMPS BM are interchangeable alternatives, not additive forces.
Qualitative scope: this study establishes that the spatial sheet runs and yields finite geometry; the quantitative confinement comparison to R1 is a followup.

baseline.name: bm-r4-coupled-2d-epithelium
baseline.note: A 2D epithelial sheet with explicit cell height, relaxed against a basement-membrane area law over the vivarium-tyssue vertex-model engine. It is the spatial counterpart of the homogeneous tissue model, so the confinement response can be read cell by cell rather than for one average cell. The current build relaxes a homogeneous sheet to finite per-cell geometry; heterogeneous growth, division and the explicit BM traction are the next additions.

robustness.note: Deterministic single configuration (one composite, no stochasticity and no parameter variation): the mesh geometry is fixed, so a single relaxation run is the whole evidence. Replication across a BM-stiffness / growth-rate sweep is a gap -- the quantitative confinement comparison to R1 (which does sweep) is a documented followup.

falsifiability: The claim would be overturned if the 2D sheet failed to resolve over the tyssue engine, if any cell-face basal area or explicit height were non-finite or non-positive after relaxation, or if stepping the EulerSolver produced a NaN or a blow-up in the per-cell geometry. Any of these would show the explicit spatial sheet does not yield well-posed geometry. The contracts in tests/test_tyssue_composites.py (test_tyssue_2d_sheet_runs) would fail in that case.

limitations: Qualitative spatial-engine check only: the study confirms the sheet runs and yields finite per-cell geometry, not that it reproduces R1's confinement regimes.

Homogeneous configuration: no heterogeneous growth, cell division or cortical-tension variation is applied, so all 12 cells relax to the same area (5.0) and height (1.93) -- the spatial heterogeneity the question asks about is not exercised yet.
The BM traction/area law (from R2) is not wired as an explicit coupling; the homogeneous-vs-spatial confinement comparison to R1 is therefore a followup, not a result.
Reduced units; single deterministic configuration (no parameter sweep, n_replicates = 1) -- replication across BM stiffness / growth rate is a gap.

config.title: R4 — 2D epithelial sheet relaxing (movie)
config.caption: Animated movie of the 12-cell 2D Tyssue sheet relaxing to its finite geometry (edges in blue). Verifies mesh construction; the planar z=0 geometry does not compute a real 3D height (see the quantitative panel + the BM-coupling gap).

config.title: 2D sheet static substrate vs R1 confinement benchmark
config.caption: MAIN (evidence: observed) — NOT a reproduction. Left: the real tyssue_2d_sheet readout over the vivarium-tyssue EulerSolver (dt 0.01) — mean per-cell basal area (fold-change vs step 0) and the stored CrossSection prism-height degree of freedom. Both are flat: all 12 cells relax to the identical basal area (5.0 reduced) and prism-height DOF (1.9319 reduced), and the max vertex displacement over the run is ~0, so the sheet is a pre-equilibrated static mesh with no spatial heterogeneity. Right: the R1 reduced-order prism benchmark (real TissuePrismProcess runs) — the confinement h/h0 trajectory for three BM regimes (soft/fast 0.998->0.38, intermediate 0.998->0.43, stiff/slow 0.998->0.70) — the confinement response the sheet does NOT reproduce. Axes dimensionless (reduced units); single deterministic run (no stochasticity). GAP (named): tyssue_2d_sheet exposes only line_tension + prefered_area — NO BM stiffness / relaxation / traction coupling — so the BM-dependent confinement regimes of Barrientos Fig 1 cannot be produced here; the right panel is the R1 benchmark, not the tyssue sheet.

config.title: 12-cell planar Tyssue mesh thumbnail (z=0)
config.caption: SUPPLEMENT (evidence: engineered-diagnostic) — a 12-cell planar Tyssue geometry resolves and relaxes on the merged CrossSectionGeometry; this verifies mesh construction but NOT BM-dependent epithelial confinement. The geometry is planar (z=0) and does NOT compute a real 3D cell height: the per-face height column is a stored CrossSection prism degree of freedom, not a resolved apical-basal distance. Reduced units; architecture/methods thumbnail only.

config.title: BM-stiffness-dependent confinement (hypothesis)
config.caption: SUPPLEMENT (evidence: hypothesis) — the BM-stiffness-dependent confinement test the figure review asked for (matched low/high-BM-relaxation cell-sheet snapshots and a basal-area-vs-time panel stratified by BM stiffness, with the R1 benchmark overlaid). NOT producible from tyssue_2d_sheet: its parameters are line_tension + prefered_area, and BM stiffness / relaxation / traction coupling is not wired into the composite. Marked hypothesis until that coupling exists.

report.title: R4 -- coupled 2D epithelial sheet (spatial substrate runs)
report.verdict: The explicit 2D epithelial sheet resolves over the vivarium-tyssue vertex-model engine and relaxes deterministically to finite, uniform per-cell geometry: 12 cell-faces at basal area 5.0 and explicit height 1.9319, stable across 5 Euler steps. This establishes the planar spatial substrate the 3D monolayer builds on. It is a qualitative engine check only -- the cells are homogeneous (no heterogeneous growth / division / BM traction), so the quantitative confinement comparison to the homogeneous R1 baseline is not yet in the composite.
report.main_insight: An explicit polygonal epithelial sheet with a per-cell height degree of freedom runs and relaxes to well-posed per-cell geometry over the tyssue engine -- the spatial substrate for the explicit confinement studies exists and is numerically stable.
report.caveat: Homogeneous relaxation with no BM traction coupling: this is a substrate-runs result, not a reproduction of the Fig 1 confinement regimes. The spatial-vs-R1 comparison is a followup.

findings.statement: The explicit 2D epithelial sheet resolves and relaxes over the tyssue engine to finite, uniform per-cell geometry: 12 cell-faces (faces = cells) and 24 vertices on a flat z=0 plane, every cell-face at basal area 5.0 and explicit height 1.9319, all finite.

evidence.observed: Nf=12, Nv=24; face area 5.0 (uniform), face height 1.9319 (uniform); all finite

findings.explanation: Each cell-face carries an explicit basal area and height degree of freedom; with no heterogeneous growth or BM traction applied, the vertex model relaxes every cell to the same well-posed geometry.
findings.next_action: use as the planar spatial substrate for the R5 3D monolayer

findings.statement: Stepping the EulerSolver five times (dt 0.01) keeps per-cell area and height finite and positive, with no NaN or blow-up -- the spatial sheet is numerically stable over short integration.

evidence.observed: per-cell area and height finite and > 0 after 5 Euler steps

findings.statement: The quantitative spatial-vs-homogeneous confinement comparison to R1 is NOT yet a result: the sheet is homogeneous (uniform cells) and the BM traction/area law is not wired as an explicit coupling, so only well-posed geometry -- not a reproduced regime -- is established.

evidence.observed: all cells identical (area 5.0, height 1.93) -- no heterogeneity or BM traction to compare against R1

findings.next_action: wire the R2-calibrated BM traction and add heterogeneous growth/division, then compare the confinement response to R1

followup_proposals.title: Wire the BM traction and compare the 2D sheet's confinement to R1
followup_proposals.motivation: The sheet currently relaxes homogeneously with no explicit BM traction, so it cannot yet test whether the Fig 1 confinement regimes survive explicit topology. Wire the R2-calibrated BM traction/area law, add heterogeneous growth / division / cortical-tension variation, and compare the per-cell confinement response to the homogeneous R1 baseline.
followup_proposals.hypothesized_mechanism: An explicit BM traction resisting basal-area growth should reproduce R1's confinement in the homogeneous limit and introduce spatial force/area heterogeneity under growth.

resolved_uncertainties: The explicit 2D epithelial sheet resolves over the tyssue engine and relaxes to finite, well-posed per-cell geometry.
The spatial sheet is numerically stable over short EulerSolver integration (no NaN / blow-up).
remaining_uncertainties: Whether the Fig 1 confinement regimes survive explicit topology -- needs the BM traction coupling and heterogeneous growth.

followup_study_proposals.title: BM traction coupling + R1 confinement comparison

regression_compatibility.basis: The tyssue_2d_sheet composite is registered and steps cleanly over the vivarium-tyssue engine; the behavior-test contracts (test_tyssue_2d_sheet_runs) pass.

biological_validation.basis: The sheet yields finite, well-posed per-cell geometry, but the figure-level confinement comparison to R1 and the BM-traction coupling are not yet in the composite, so no biological regime is validated or refuted here.

explanatory_gain.basis: Establishes that an explicit spatial epithelial substrate runs and is numerically stable; it does not yet add biological understanding of confinement beyond the homogeneous R1 model.

expert_questions: Is the homogeneous relaxation (uniform cells, no BM traction) a sufficient substrate milestone, or should the R1 confinement comparison be a blocking requirement before R4 is called evidence?
Should the BM traction be wired as an effective constitutive law (continuous with R1) or as an explicit LAMMPS coupling before the spatial confinement claim is made?
